The plaintiff is before the court for the following relief:
a) To declare that the plaintiff is the absolute owner of the disputed encroached portion of the property measuring approximately East-West 6 feet and North to South 60 feet, and that the same is part and parcel of the registered sale deed dated 4-6- 1987.

b) Perpetual injunction against the defendants, restraining them, their agents, servants, or anyone claiming under them from interfering with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit property.

c) Mandatory injunction against the defendants, directing them to remove the construction in the area of 660 feet all along the eastern side of the suit property encroached upon by them, and in the event of their failure to comply with such direction, to order the same to be demolished and restore the plaintiff to possession of the same.

d) Such other order or orders as this court may be pleased to pass in the circumstances of the case,
including an order as to costs in the interest of justice and equity.
2. In the suit, it is contended that the plaintiff is the absolute owner in possession and enjoyment of the schedule property.

The plaintiff purchased Site Nos. 195 and 196 from her vendor Aisha Qamar under the registered sale deed dated 4-6-1987, and subsequently had her name entered in the records of the Corporation of the City of Bangalore as per the endorsement dated 15-10-1987.
She has constructed a residential house as per the sanctioned plan and has been living there with her family.
The entire area in and around the property was originally revenue property.
The Bangalore Development Authority acquired the same and formed a layout.
Site Nos. 195 and 196 were allotted to Smt. Aisha Qamar under a possession certificate.

The said Site Nos. 195 and 196 were separate,
and by a rectification deed dated 20-8-1984, both were clubbed together and common boundaries were mentioned.
3. A perusal of Annexure F shows that on the eastern side of the suit property, there is a road.
This was originally occupied by hut dwellers but has now been cleared for a pucca road.
On the eastern side of the property, there are no other properties -- only the road.
As the huts are being cleared, the formation of the road has been delayed, as can be seen from the sketch.
The plaintiff has a vacant space of 10 feet in depth, measuring 1060 feet.

The defendants have started encroaching upon the Gowramma R vs Krishnappa on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128956453/
4 said strip by illegally occupying a portion measuring 660 feet all along the eastern side of the schedule property and are now making preparations for putting up a compound wall.
For this purpose, the defendants collected men and materials on the morning of 17-4-1991.
The plaintiff protested against the construction but to no avail.
As demonstrated by the documents of title and the rectification deed, there are no properties on the eastern side of the schedule property except the road.
The defendants have no manner of right, title, or interest to encroach upon the property of the plaintiff, much less put up a permanent structure.
If the defendants are not prohibited from putting up a permanent structure on the schedule property, irreparable damage will be caused.
4. It is submitted that the defendants were trying to encroach upon the strip measuring 660 feet all along the eastern side of the property.
This court was pleased to grant an interim temporary injunction against the defendants, restraining them from interfering with the schedule property.

Despite the injunction against them, the defendants encroached upon the scheduled property on the eastern side to the extent of 660 feet all along the eastern side of the suit property and further put up construction in that area.
The defendants have no manner of right, title, or interest to encroach upon the property.
Hence, the defendants ought to be directed to remove the encroachment.
5. The plaintiff, being the owner in possession and enjoyment, has a prima facie case in her favour.
The defendants have no right on the eastern side, as that area is reserved only for a road.
Further, if the defendants put up a permanent structure, the plaintiff will lose her valuable property.

Hence,
this is a fit case wherein the court may be pleased to exercise its discretion in favour of preventing the defendants from carrying out their illegal activity by granting an injunction, which will cause no injury to the defendants as they have no right, title, or interest therein.
6. The cause of action arose on 17-4-1991 within the jurisdiction of this court.
With these contentions, the plaintiff has prayed for the above-said reliefs.
7. Defendant No. 3 filed a written statement denying and disputing the plaint allegations.

8. In the written statement, it is contended that the suit schedule site was formed by the BDA and, as the BDA has not been made a party to this suit, the same is liable to be dismissed.
9.

The property in Sy. No. 73/4 of Akkithimmannahalli originally belonged to Sri C.T. Ramanna, the father of this and the other defendants, and in the year 1963 was notified for acquisition by the City Improvement Trust and was finally acquired.
10. After acquiring and taking possession of the property, the BDA formed a layout and allotted suit sites to the plaintiff's predecessor in title.
The BDA has allotted an alternate site bearing No. 214/A of the same layout to the defendants.
However, the BDA has not put the defendant in possession of the site allotted to them, and this defendant is also not residing next to the suit property.
It is submitted that the allegation that the defendant encroached is not correct.
The defendant has no right over the plaintiff's portion of her property as alleged, as the BDA has not issued a possession certificate to the defendant.
There is no cause of action, and the suit is liable to be dismissed.

With Gowramma R vs Krishnappa on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128956453/
5 these contentions, Defendant No. 3 has prayed for dismissal of the suit.

12. It is contended that Defendant No. 1 is the owner of the property bearing Sy. No. 73/3,
measuring 70 feet x 130 feet, in Corporation Division No. 64, in Shanti Nagar, Akkithimmannahalli,
purchased from one Srikanta Shastry under a registered sale deed, and since then the defendant has been in possession and enjoyment of the property as absolute owner.
Neither the plaintiff nor any person claiming through her has any rights over an inch of the property.
13. The plaintiff, being an influential woman in the locality, is making attempts to encroach upon the property of Defendant No. 1, who is in peaceful possession.
Defendant No. 1, who is a respectable man in the locality, could not withstand the conduct of the plaintiff.
The plaintiff, taking the law into her own hands and considering the defendants to be law-abiding citizens, is trying to profit from the same.
There is no necessity for the plaintiff to encroach upon any property of the defendant or anyone else.
The plaintiff was not given the survey number of the property to ascertain the actual measurement of her property.
The plaintiff has made false allegations against the defendant solely to harass them and to claim the property of the defendant.
The suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed.

14. The defendant has not made any disturbance or set up any persons to claim the property of the plaintiff; on the contrary, the plaintiff has adopted such tactics to grab the property of Defendant No. 1, who is the absolute owner.
The suit on hand, brought by the plaintiff, is not maintainable, as the plaintiff must get a survey of the property owned by her to ascertain the actual measurement.
15. Therefore, Defendant No. 1, being the absolute owner of the property in question, has not relinquished any right in the property claimed in the plaint.

The plaintiff has no right over the property measuring 6 feet by 60 feet as claimed in the plaint, as Defendant No. 1 is in actual physical possession of the entire property measuring 70 feet by 130 feet.

As such, the plaintiff is put to strict proof of her case, and a survey of both the plaintiff's and Defendant No. 1's property should be conducted to ascertain the truth and actual measurement of the property in their respective possession.

16. The claim of the plaintiff is imaginary and inconsistent with the actual rights of Defendant No. 1 in the property, who is in actual possession and occupation of the property measuring 70 feet by 130 feet.

Therefore, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed with exemplary costs, as the plaintiff has no nexus to the property in question as claimed in the plaint, and Defendant No. 1 is the absolute owner.
With these grounds, Defendants No. 1 and 2 have prayed for rejection of the suit.

In the circumstances, the case of the plaintiff is not sustainable and has to be dismissed with exemplary costs.

Instead, three endorsements dated 16-10-2024 were issued, stating that the particulars sought with regard to Site Nos. 197, 208, and 209 are not matters of public importance but are third-party related issues, and that the BDA cannot furnish the required particulars sought in the applications of these defendants.

Hence, these defendants sought this court to revisit its previous reasoning while dismissing the application filed by them, observing that they could approach the RTI authority of the BDA to meet their requirements.

The BDA has virtually played fraud upon the court by not choosing to produce the required particulars sought by these defendants in their earlier application filed before this court, and by withholding the documents instead of producing the same.
33. Admittedly, this court, while disposing of the related RFA for further appropriate trial, noted the culpable acts of the BDA as having dragged the parties into litigation.

The dual conduct of the BDA in filing objections to the earlier application and the action taken on the RTI application filed by these defendants has prolonged the matter and caused the parties to litigate for more than three decades.
Under these circumstances, this court must require the BDA to discharge its duties and responsibilities without concealing anything in the subject matter, so as to enable the court to render justice.

The unlawful acts of the BDA in preparing an erroneous layout plan contrary to the actual existence of sites has caused the parties to the suit to fight on account of its own misconduct.
The inaction and attitude of the BDA has failed to create a conducive atmosphere for resolution of the issue.
The dual conduct of the BDA in filing objections to the earlier application and the action taken on the RTI application filed by these defendants has prolonged the matter and caused the parties to litigate for more than three decades.
Under these circumstances, this court must require the BDA to discharge its duties and responsibilities without concealing anything in the subject matter, so as to enable the court to render justice.
